summary: Proceed. This is a sound stage-4 rewrite aimed at the limiter DIAGNOSIS names: L2->SM activation ingest on rega's 128x128 tile. It is the reviewer-named successor to the flat pingpong run. One build-plan defect could make a failure unreadable, so it must be fixed before the build: folding the new kernel into master's rega module puts master's own ft and high rega at risk through build time and failure.
justification: Mechanism. Master's rega_kernel works like this (submission.py ~2812-2970): a 128-weight-row tile (8 consumer warps x 16 rows); per k-stage 9216 B of weight plus up to 32768 B of bf16 slab (STAGE_BYTES 41984); the dequant is serialised with the MMA (wgmma_wait<0> right after each commit, 'variant A'); the slab is re-read once per 128-row tile. Pairing two adjacent tiles over the same chunk halves the activation bytes issued per FLOP (about 25 B/clk of MMA instead of about 41) without touching the bank, align or chunk tables. The wait<1> schedule across two register-A sets is correct: each set is rewritten only after its own group has retired, and each stage is released after B(n-1) retires. The k16 order per output is unchanged, so bit-exactness is the right gate. The resources fit. Dynamic smem is 189440 B plus at most about 14.3 KB static, under 227 KB. setmaxnreg 40x128 + 232x256 = 64512 registers. Three stages of 2x MMA work buffer about 6K clk, against master's about 4K. The profile backs the targets. rega<true,true> is 3652-3848 us and rega<false,true> 1851-1890 us on the first_turn rows; at turn_4 rega w13/w2 are 741/357 us (sliding) and 763/370 us (full). That is about 1.75x the 989-TFLOP/s floor, so a <=2900/<=1450 us target is physically reachable. turn_1 stays on the low class, so 'unchanged' there is a valid control. Weakest link: the evidence that L2->SM ingest is a hard ceiling is inferential. Pingpong being slower at 4.76 TB/s fits either an ingest cap or a latency/issue cap. The 2-CTA V64 low class (LESSONS) reached about 6.4 TB/s and ran 12% faster, so 5.8-6.05 TB/s was not a hard wall; part of the cap may be per-CTA latency/occupancy, which a bigger tile with fewer resident warps does not fix. Second weakest: two 64-fp32 accumulator sets + 64 A registers + addressing + the silu epilogue, under 232 registers. The w13 NB=128 instantiation may spill or be wgmma-serialised by ptxas; the plan already prints both and turns the variant OFF. Prior check: the hypothesis has no 'prior' field. Its closest relatives are the pingpong (consumer overlap on the 128-row tile, Do-not-try 'until actions 1 or 2 remove the cap') and producer-scale-expand runs, both flat because the tile was ingest-capped. This change attacks the cap itself; DIAGNOSIS explicitly names it as action 2 and exempts it, so the difference is real and it is not a repeat. Stale facts in the brief: it says base 1932a9c4 and prepare ~124 s. Master is now 61ce79bb (combo B over combo A: fused norm-gather, the rega_lo module, FA3 contiguous gather), and prepare reaches 139.9 s before the rega-lo phase ends. _experts_rega now takes prenorm/variant arguments. The builder must rebase onto the current master.
confounders: experts-turn-rega-s4-port-t4096 + experts-turn-rega-s4-first-turn-n128 (the incumbent rega module): the plan compiles _rega_src() + the wide string under a bumped name (muse_prefill_rega_v3). Master's high and ft rega then depend on the new code compiling and on the longer nvcc time. If it fails, the plan rebuilds v2 (about 38 s more). Either way prepare can pass REGA_FT_START_DEADLINE_S = 150 s (ft-self-check already ends at about 120 s, and combo B added time). That would turn master's ft rega OFF and send first_turn back to Triton (0.63x slower), a large regression that looks like the wide kernel failing. Fix in the change: build the wide kernel as a SEPARATE module (as rega_lo is) AFTER master's rega/ft setup, leaving muse_prefill_rega_v2 byte-identical. Wide must never be a prerequisite of master's path.

combo-b-normgather-two-cta-low-regate: adds the rega_lo build and gate (33.2 s; prepare total 139.9 s) and does not interact with the high/ft kernels. It is the main source of prepare-budget pressure for the new build and gates under REGA_BUDGET_S 200 / REGA_COPY_DEADLINE_S 255. Print the prepare total before and after the wide phase.

combo-a-master-normgather-naive-stack (pre-expert norm fused into rega gather): the wide kernel reads the same xs slab through the same TMA maps, so there is no numeric interaction. Its gate should time the norm-gather-ON block (as rega-lo did) or the GEMM kernels alone, so the ratio is not diluted by gather time.

align-two-phase-all-t-rega: supplies the chunk/block tables the wide kernel reuses unchanged. Halving n_tiles halves the item count with longer items, so the persistent-grid tail at high-class w2 (about 1024 mixed bucket-128/64 items over 132 CTAs) roughly doubles in us. This is an interaction with the chunking, not with align itself, and the per-class gate absorbs it.
interference: No companion. This is kind: rewrite, and its result is read from per-kernel times and PATH CHOSEN lines, which the gate prints for both variants per class. A companion check would add nothing that prepare cannot print for free. The one attribution question is whether a gain comes from halved ingest or from the in-warpgroup dequant/MMA overlap. That is best answered inside prepare: if build time allows, time a diagnostic instantiation of the wide kernel with wait<0> after each group (no overlap; print-only, never ON) at ft for w2. The landed confounders are all handled by fixing the build coupling (separate module) rather than by an ab-revert. The queued experts-rega-mc2-slab-multicast-all-t attacks the same limiter by another route and should run in the same batch, per DIAGNOSIS: mc2 faster + wide faster confirms ingest; wide faster + pingpong flat confirms the overlap was ingest-masked.
rules_flags: None blocking. Weights stay NVFP4/E4M3 in global memory and are dequantized in registers, with BF16 activations and fp32 accumulation. Outputs are bit-identical to master. kernel_fn dispatches only on T and prepare flags. Per-state Maps/bank/error word are kept with no module globals. Every route is computed.

Gate rigor, not a rule: today's LESSONS line (single-round 1.02x selectors mis-routed bf16) asks for two interleaved rounds, both meeting the threshold (<=0.97 here), with a candidate IQR bound against master's. The hypothesis specifies one round of REGA_ALTERNATIONS at <=0.97. Adopt the two-round rule. Note also that master's own rega gate uses REGA_GATE_RATIO 0.95.
open_questions: Will the build go into a separate module after master's ft setup (recommended) instead of the bumped muse_prefill_rega_v3 that replaces v2? If not, what is the measured ft start time with the larger TU, and the time on the build-failure-then-v2 path, against the 150 s REGA_FT_START_DEADLINE_S?

Does w13 NB=128 fit under 232 registers with no spill and no 'wgmma serialization' warning? fence_acc must touch only the accumulator set NOT in flight, or ptxas will serialise. If w13 spills, does w2-only still clear 0.97 at ft?
At high class (T=3012), does the doubled per-item cost with about 1024 mixed-bucket w2 items on 132 CTAs eat the gain through tail imbalance? Print items per CTA, min/max.

Is about 6 TB/s really the L2->SM ceiling? Print the wide kernel's issued TB/s next to master's. If wide stays at about 6 TB/s while its time drops, ingest was the cap. If its TB/s drops and time is flat, the limiter is latency/issue and stage 5 should pivot (e.g. to the PDL chain or the 2-CTA/multicast idea).
The gate routings at 3012/16384 are soft/random. Chunking is unchanged, so skew sensitivity should be small, but print one skewed-routing ratio as a guard, as combo B's lesson suggests.
